q1_issues.issue: The copular indefinite 'a kilo of ketchup' is parsed as a specific witness at individual-fact confidence 0.99, whereas the instruction set makes indefinite 'a/an' generic in a copular/definitional predication, so a general conversion claim is recorded as a fact about one particular quantity.

q2_gaps: measure of-phrase ('a kilo of ketchup', 'a cup of water') - named only as an exclusion from the possessive of-phrase rule, with no positive encoding specified
generic over a measured quantity - the copular-indefinite generic rule has no kind symbol available for 'a kilo of X', so no kind-level form of this claim is expressible
notes: Equivalent + (Symmetric Equivalent) is licensed by the stative symmetric-predicate rule ('is similar / equal / married to'), and the aggregate Measure on the tomato group follows the plural-measure rule.
